FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Military System Refactor
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description:
This update features a hefty refactor of Empire's military system, largely in the name of future extensibility. Some of the changes won't be evident to the player, but many will; and in time, this refactor should allow for further new and requested features.

This update *does* make some fairly substantial changes to how squads work. If you don't like those changes -- or any of the other changes -- then the latest 1.3.x version of Empire will be available in the releases section of the official Empire Refactored github. But once 1.5.x hits the steam workshop, support for 1.3.x will cease.

1.5.x should be save compatible with previous versions, but active battles or military events might behave a little weirdly.

patchNoteLines.li: Auto-resolve battles now play out round-by-round over time, complete with a window to watch the battle's progress. Now you can see all of the RNG and math that goes into determining an auto-resolve result.
Battle Reports for both auto- and manual-battles are archived in the Military main tab. Reports for auto-battles include the round-by-round progress.
Multiple simultaneous attacks on the same settlement are now supported. The mod currently doesn't actually *use* this behavior, but it opens the door to lots of fun stuff in the future.
The reward for an Overwhelming Victory has been changed from cooldown elimination to a small happiness and loyalty boost.

Added Crushing Defeat, the opposite of Overwhelming Victory. A Crushing Defeat is when you're defeated without inflicting a single casualty on the opposing force. The penalties for Crushing Defeat are more severe than for regular defeats.

Squads have been completely reworked. No longer do you design a squad and then assign it to a settlement for free. Now, you must hire each individual squad. Furthermore, squads will not automatically update if you change their associated template; you have to pay to update them. And if a member of the squad dies, you'll need to hire a replacement. Squads aren't a free lunch anymore, pal!
(There are options in the settings to reduce the hire/upgrade cost for squads. If you *really* hate paying for things, you can drop the costs to 0, to emulate older Empire behavior.)
Injured squad members will heal over time. A squad that is deployed with injured members will not be as effective as when it's completely healthy.
All deployments and offensive operations cost 20% of the squad's value. This was technically already true for deployments, but this update surfaces that cost in the UI and sends you a bill.
Post-deployment squad cooldowns have been mostly replaced with travel time based on the distance back to their home settlement.

You can now personally customize each squad by editing the loadouts of specific squad members, or hiring additional members to a specific squad. All of these changes flow naturally into a squad's effective power, currently calculated from the squad's total value.
Settlements without an assigned squad will defend at half-power when attacked.
There is now support for a settlement to host multiple squads. The mod itself doesn't take advantage of this yet, but it opens some neat doors for the future.

New UI for picking squads to defend a settlement, or to attack an enemy settlement. Estimated enemy power and each squad's estimated win chance are now surfaced in the UI, so offensive operations aren't blind anymore.
Non-Empire NPC settlements now show their estimated military level and efficiency when selected on the world map.
Deployed squads will now immediately follow new orders instead of finishing their previous order first.
Bills can now carry custom late- and unpaid-payment penalties, used for mercenary deployment bills currently.

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Minor Refactors
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Various minor backend refactors to clean up the code. There shouldn't be any impact on gameplay.

patchNoteLines.li: Various backend refactors

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Xenotype Cost Modifier Change
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Changes the cost modifier for xenotypes in the Unit Template maker. Previously, the modifier just multiplied together all of the xenotype's genes' non-zero marketValueFactors. Now, we take various other stats into account: metabolism, complexity, archites, how many abilities the gene grants, stat bonuses, pain bonus, damage resist. All individually weighted with settings sliders.\n\nThe effect from each gene is also added together instead of multiplied. The cost of a xenotype shouldn't explode quite so easily anymore, but supremely powerful xenotypes will still be very expensive.

patchNoteLines.li: Rework the xenotype cost calculation for merc units

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Backend Refactors
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Some backend reorganization of the code. Player-facing functionality should not be affected.

patchNoteLines.li: Create a FindFC class, similar to Verse.Find
Pull Tax and Event code out of the FactionFC World Component

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: More Backend Updates
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Some backend code changes to clean things up. User-facing functionality should not change.

patchNoteLines.li: Backend code changes

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Prisoner Update
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: A polish and balance pass for prisoners.

patchNoteLines.li: Adds a prisoner tab to the main tab window, giving an overview of all prisoners in your empire
Prisoners now lose health on a daily basis, instead of on each tax tick
Downed prisoners do not grant a worker bonus
Prisoners at full health no longer magically regrow their legs
Prisoners must be physically transported to the destination settlement and then transfer via world map gizmo. No more magical teleportation

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Merc Needs Fix
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Hardens some of the checks in ResetNeeds to prevent weird modded races from throwing errors.

patchNoteLines.li: Check RaceProps.Humanlike instead of !AnimalOrWildMan

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: More Caching
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Makes more use of Def caching. Will this actually produce a notable performance improvement? I doubt it. But at least all our Def grabbing is in one place! ...Just, don't ever hot-reload your defs, please.

patchNoteLines.li: Adds more Def caching to FactionCache

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Vehicle Framework Compat Fix
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Fixes an issue where joining a manual battle with a vehicle and never dismounting the pawns inside can result in both getting silently purged when the battle is over.

patchNoteLines.li: When checking for battle end-state, loop over AllPawnsSpawned with a Faction.OfPlayer filter instead of looping over FreeColonistsSpawned

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Prisoners Update 2
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Adds some quality-of-life features to prisoner handling, and also a slight balance pass.

patchNoteLines.li: Adds buttons to set the default prisoner workload on a faction and per-settlement basis
Adds buttons to bulk set prisoner workloads on a faction and per-settlement basis
Multiple prisoner deaths at the same settlement are bundled into one letter
Prisoner deaths now grant a -2 relations penalty with the prisoner's home faction

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: No-map Edge case fix
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Fixes an edge-case scenario where tax delivery would error out if the player has no active maps. Technically possible with caravans/nomadic playthroughs.

patchNoteLines.li: Patch DeliveryEvent.Action to check the TaxMap early; if null, go through the safe handling route in PaymentUtil

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Event Cost Scaling
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Adds a mod option to scale the silver cost of event options, just in case the values are too low (or high) for your liking.

patchNoteLines.li: Adds a mod option to scale silver costs of event options

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Event Update
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Various tweaks and edits to random events.

patchNoteLines.li: Various tweaks and edits to random events

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Minor Military Changes
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Before, the strength of a settlement's defending force was snapshot at the moment a warning letter is sent, and that snapshot is carried forward into the battle. This means that any changes to military level or combat efficiency during the warning window wouldn't actually apply to the coming battle.\n\nThis update changes that. Now, the defending force's strength is recalculated at battle start.

patchNoteLines.li: Recalculate defender strength at the start of a defense battle

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Events Balance Pass
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: A broad balance pass to make events harder to cheese: when an event has options, the game auto-pauses and can't be unpaused or saved until an option is chosen. Additionally, the base cost of event options now scales by the number of settlements affected, among other things.

patchNoteLines.li: Force-pause the game when an event with options pops
Scale event option costs by the number of affected settlements, as well as optionally by faction income or resource production
General balance and editing pass for all events

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Fix for pawn generation in battles
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Adds protection against failed GeneratePawn calls fouling up the map generation for a manual defense battle, which would then crash the game.

patchNoteLines.li: In BattlefieldContext.RecruitMapInhabitants, move the GeneratePawn call into the try/catch block

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: No 3rd-party hostiles in manual defense
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: When generating a manual defense battle, we now loop through all things and destroy any that are hostile to the player. This loop runs before adding hostiles, and is necessary to clean the map of third-party hostiles such as if the settlement was founded on a Launch Point landmark.

patchNoteLines.li: When setting up a defense battle in BattlefieldContext.StartDefense, strip third-party hostiles after generating the map but before setting up the actual attack

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: Compatibility Update
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Update the choose-a-defender dialog to be able to handle defenders from other mods (such as the eventual Vanilla Outposts Expanded compat patch).

patchNoteLines.li: Update Dialog_DefendSettlement to handle non-WorldSettlementFC defenders

FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.label: PlanetTile Update
FactionColonies.PatchNoteDef.description: Updates IRaidTarget to use PlanetTile instead of int.

patchNoteLines.li: Updates IRaidTarget to use PlanetTile instead of int
